granola-vs-otter-ai.0: Granola vs Otter AI is really a choice between two ideas of what a meeting note taker should be. One is a transcription engine. Otter records everything, shows words on screen as people speak, and summarizes afterwards; Granola is a notebook that listens quietly on your device and turns your shorthand into full notes.
granola-vs-otter-ai.1: In the Granola vs Otter AI decision, both tools are good. They just suit different people. This guide compares them on capture, pricing, privacy, and what you get after the call.
granola-vs-otter-ai.2: Capture is the main difference. Otter sends a meeting agent into your Zoom, Google Meet or Teams call and transcribes live, while Granola never joins the call and works from your device's audio. One keeps the full transcript; the other focuses on the notes.
granola-vs-otter-ai.3: Want a word-for-word record you can search later? That is what Otter is built for. If you would rather have concise notes in your own structure, that is Granola's job.
granola-vs-otter-ai.4: On annual billing, Otter is cheaper ($8.33 a month for Pro), while Granola is simpler ($14 a month for Business, no minute caps). Team plans flip the comparison, because Otter Business costs $19.99 a user billed yearly, which puts it above Granola Business.
granola-vs-otter-ai.5: With Otter Pro you get 1,200 minutes a month, and each conversation is capped at 90 minutes. No Granola plan lists a minute cap at all. Full details: [Granola pricing](https://lynkk.ai/blog/granola-pricing).
granola-vs-otter-ai.6: For occasional short calls, Otter's free plan works: 300 minutes a month, though each conversation stops at 30 minutes and only your 25 most recent conversations are kept. Frequent meetings with short-term memory suit Granola's free plan better. No minute cap. Just 30 days of history.
granola-vs-otter-ai.8: Privacy goes to Granola. It never adds a bot to the meeting, does not keep video, and lets every plan opt out of model training. Otter's bot, by contrast, is visible to every attendee, which is transparent but can raise client concerns.
granola-vs-otter-ai.9: On the enterprise side, Otter's top plan adds SSO, SCIM and a HIPAA compliance add-on, and Granola's Enterprise adds SSO, org-wide auto-deletion and team-wide training opt-out. Whichever you choose, tell attendees you are taking AI notes. Several US states require consent from everyone on a recorded call.
granola-vs-otter-ai.10: Sales teams that want a full record should look at Otter: Pro adds Salesforce, HubSpot and Zapier integrations, and Enterprise includes an Otter Sales Notetaker. Founders and small sales teams that want notes, not recordings, often prefer Granola Business, which connects to HubSpot, Attio and Affinity.
granola-vs-otter-ai.11: Coaching reps from transcripts? Otter wins. Selling in relationship-driven calls where a bot feels awkward is a different story, and there Granola fits better.
granola-vs-otter-ai.12: In-person meetings are covered by both, through mobile apps. Granola handles in-person conversations on iPhone and, since July 2026, on Android. On Otter, the mobile apps record in person on free and paid plans alike.
granola-vs-otter-ai.13: There is a catch with Otter's in-person recordings: they count toward the same 300 or 1,200 monthly minutes. Granola's do not have a minute cap. So for in-person interviews longer than 30 minutes, Otter's free plan will cut off.
granola-vs-otter-ai.14: In clear audio, each tool produces usable English transcripts, and each struggles with crosstalk, heavy accents and poor microphones. What differs is how much the transcript matters: it is Otter's main output, whereas Granola uses it as raw material to write notes.
granola-vs-otter-ai.17: Out of the box, Otter connects to more tools: Salesforce, HubSpot and Zapier on Pro, plus an API and webhooks on Enterprise. Granola Business names 5 (Attio, Notion, HubSpot, Affinity and Zapier) and adds MCP and API access.
granola-vs-otter-ai.19: There are 2 different ways these tools capture meetings, and that one difference explains most of what users notice. Otter's meeting agent joins the call as a participant and records from inside the meeting. Granola, on the other hand, listens to your computer's audio output and microphone. It hears what you hear.
granola-vs-otter-ai.22: Your own notes drive Granola's summaries. Type "pricing objection" and "follow up Tuesday" during the call, and the summary is organized around those points, with detail filled in from the transcript. Otter's summaries follow the conversation instead: an overview, key topics and action items in the order they came up.
granola-vs-otter-ai.23: Neither style is better in every case. People who already know what matters in a meeting tend to like Granola's approach. When you were not paying close attention, or when someone else needs the full picture, Otter's approach works better. Either way, check names, numbers and owners before you send a summary on.
granola-vs-otter-ai.24: A lot changed in 2026. Granola launched an Android app on 1 July 2026 for in-person conversations, and its Business plan now lists an MCP integration and API access. Over at Otter, the pricing page now lists an Otter Sales Notetaker on Enterprise, a HIPAA compliance add-on, and promotional Pro pricing for India-issued cards.
granola-vs-otter-ai.27: Company age shows in the product. More integrations and enterprise features on one side; a narrower, more opinionated design on the other.
granola-vs-otter-ai.28: Teams that want both styles in one tool often look at Lynkk (our product). It offers a bot for Zoom, Google Meet and Teams, the way Otter does, and bot-free recording through a Mac app and Chrome extension, the way Granola does. In-person conversations are covered too.
granola-vs-otter-ai.32: Choose Otter if you want live transcripts, an automatic bot, Salesforce or HubSpot integration on Pro, or the lowest annual price at $8.33 a month. Private, bot-free notes that start from your own typing, with no minute caps, point to Granola. And if you want both capture modes plus the follow-up work done for you, choose Lynkk.
granola-vs-otter-ai.34: It depends on what you need. For private, bot-free notes with no minute caps, Granola is better. For live transcripts, automatic recording and CRM integrations, Otter wins. The real question is whether you want notes or a full record, so test both on the same 3 meetings.
granola-vs-otter-ai.35: Yes. Otter remains a strong transcription tool with live captions, speaker identification and integrations. Its main drawbacks are the 30-minute cap on free conversations and the visible bot. Upgrading to Pro raises the per-conversation limit to 90 minutes and adds Salesforce, HubSpot and Zapier integrations for $8.33 a month on annual billing.
granola-vs-otter-ai.36: Not quite. Granola transcribes your meeting audio to write notes, but it does not show a live transcript on screen the way Otter does. What you get is structured notes rather than a word-for-word transcript view, so if you need to quote exact words later, Otter's transcript view suits you better.
granola-vs-otter-ai.37: Pro costs $16.99 a month on monthly billing or $8.33 a month billed yearly. Business costs $30 a month or $19.99 billed yearly. The Basic plan is free with 300 minutes a month. Annual billing roughly halves Otter Pro's monthly price.
granola-vs-otter-ai.39: Otter's agent joins Microsoft Teams meetings directly. Granola captures Teams calls through its Mac or Windows desktop app instead. Both work, though only Otter needs nothing open on your machine. For client calls, Granola is the quieter option, because no bot appears in the participant list.
